title: capacity-urgency-scanner-and-deadband-orchestrator
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight urgency scoring pipeline and deadband orchestrator to reduce autoscaler churn while improving guaranteed throughput during spike sequences. Metrics and opt-in canary enabled.
description:
Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets sometimes oscillate when microbursts overlap with gradual reservation changes. The autoscaler reacts to short-lived utilization spikes and then immediately decommits which causes downstream tail-latency regressions and lost throughput guarantees. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) Capacity Urgency Scanner - a streaming, low-cost scorer that synthesizes latency SLO misses, reservation exhaustion signals, and short-window token pressure into a single urgency metric; (2) Deadband Orchestrator - a hysteresis/deadband layer that gates scale decisions using the urgency score plus a stochastic smoothing window to avoid flip-flopping on borderline signals. Goals: reduce unnecessary scale-outs/ins by >= 25% in microburst-heavy traffic, preserve 95th/99th latency SLOs during scale transitions, and provide observability for post-mortem and tuning.

What changed (high level): added the urgency scanner pipeline in pkg/autoscale/urgency, new deadband orchestrator in pkg/autoscale/deadband, telemetry hooks (metrics + events) in observability layer, a lightweight unit/integration test harness under test/autoscale, and a canary job config for benchmark-lab to exercise microburst patterns.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-1420)
- [x] Unit tests for scorer and policy rules
- [x] Integration test against perf-canary scenarios
- [x] Prometheus metrics + Grafana dashboard panel suggestion
- [x] Opt-in feature flag for dedicated clusters
- [x] Release note drafted

Summary of commits: single logical feature implemented with small refactors to existing autoscaler interfaces, split across 7 commits. See commits list for topical breakdown.

Changed areas / files (high-level):
- pkg/autoscale/urgency/scanner.go (new): implements moving-window urgency calculator, exposes CalculateUrgency(poolID, samples) -> float64
- pkg/autoscale/deadband/orchestrator.go (new): deadband state machine, policy rules, backoff timer, and cross-pool coordination hooks
- pkg/autoscale/policy/adapter.go (mod): thin adapter to allow existing autoscaler to consume urgency->action signals
- observability/metrics/registrations.go (mod): new metrics registrations for capacity_urgency_score, deadband_state, deadband_transitions_total
- test/autoscale/fixtures/* (new): synthetic trace fixtures for microburst/reservation patterns
- benchmark-lab/canary/urgency-deadband.yml (new): canary job to run microburst trace sets against dedicated cluster
- docs/ops/autoscaler-tuning.md (mod): guidance and knobs for tuning urgency thresholds and deadband windows
- scripts/perf/checks.sh (mod): integrate canary validation step into CI (opt-in)

Small illustrative snippet added (scanner window core):
```\n// urgency computed as weighted sum: latencyVio + max(0, reservationShortfall) * burstFactor\nu := 0.6*latencyScore + 0.4*math.Max(0, reservationShortfall)*burstFactor\n```

Telemetry and observability: new metrics exported under the redwood.autoscale namespace: capacity_urgency_score{pool}, deadband_state{pool}, deadband_transition{pool,from,to}, urgency_sample_latency_bucket. Events emitted to tracing when deadband opens/closes so SRE can inspect decision timelines. Grafana panel JSON included in docs/ops/autoscaler-tuning.md as a suggested dashboard.

Performance and canary results: ran benchmark-lab canary against a dedicated test pool with microburst trace set v2. Results: autoscaler churn (scale in/out toggles per hour) reduced 32% versus baseline; 95th token latency improved by 12% during transitions. Canary logs attached in CI artifacts (build/archives/urgency-canary-2026-02-21.tar.gz).

Review conversation summary: reviewers requested clearer separation of scoring normalization and policy thresholds, and a defensive check to avoid negative reservationShortfall causing counter-intuitive boosts. Addressed by commit 5 which adds normalization utilities and clamps intermediate signals. Also added a feature flag for opt-in rollout per-cluster. Security reviewed; no secrets or new external network paths introduced. Backwards compat: autoscaler adapter default behavior preserves existing scaling decisions when feature flag is off.

CI: all unit/integration tests pass in the redwood CI pipeline. Perf-canary is opt-in and was run manually during verification. Linter required a couple of small style fixes which were amended.

Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge after signoff from Amit and Lina. Post-merge actions: created a follow-up ticket ENG-1973 to expose a tuning UI in the console and track customer feedback from early adopters. Feature rolled out to a small set of Dedicated customers under an opt-in flag for two weeks to validate signals in production.

review_comments: Amit Shah: Can we separate normalization from scoring? The current weights are hard-coded and will be confusing in future tuning. Requested: move weights into config and add a normalization util.
Marisol Vega (author): Addressed in commit 5 — moved weights into autoscale/config and added NormalizeSignal() with unit tests. Also added a short doc section on safe ranges.
Lina Perez: Add a defensive clamp so negative reservationShortfall can't amplify urgency due to math errors. Also please ensure metrics don't create cardinality explosion.
Marisol Vega (author): Added clamp and histogram bucketing for urgency samples. Cardinality note: we tag metrics only by pool and zone; no per-tenant tags are emitted.
Theo Martin: Approve after canary results and CI green. Asked for a follow-up to expose tuning in console.
Marisol Vega (author): Follow-up created ENG-1973 to track console exposure and customer telemetry collection. Thanks for the review.
